title: Generative UI, semantic compilation and shared state — session summary
status: open — next topic: how an LLM 'listens'

facts: Launched with GPT-6 on 2026-10-07 (paid tiers; Free/Go from 10-08), Chat tab only
Official: library of native streamable components + compiler that renders progressively; model trained to judge layout
reverse_engineered_by_thesys_unconfirmed: Model writes DIL (Markdown + JSX-like tags + JS state); server recompiles full program every ~250ms, repairs partial output, validates props against catalog
Client runs program in sandboxed iframe + locked-down worker; native renderer accepts only known component types
Server-resolved data (images, products, citations, tool-result bindings) — model never retypes values
Only path UI -> model is issueNewTurn (a plain user message); model cannot see UI state; state lost on reload
AppBlock = open-ended HTML escape hatch in sandboxed iframe
openai_intelligent_ui.assessment: Today mostly frame selection among ~70 components; looks nicer, little AI benefit yet. Real leap needs UI state the model can see, persistence, stable schemas.

observstory.principle: State belongs to the project. Form belongs to the projection.
observstory.pipeline: observations (impure) -> derive -> snapshot (typed) -> map_compiler -> scene IR (zone/group/node/edge + attention, details; no coordinates) -> renderer
observstory.adapts_to: project state and shape (lanes, overlap, waiting, freeze), not viewer or question; at build time, not live
observstory.ui_evolution: radar (read as dashboard) -> Project Map + scene contract (ADR-023) -> draw-once rule (ADR-024) -> mission rail above map (ADR-032) -> renderer-only density fixes (ADR-033)
observstory.ai_hook_named_not_built: FrameIntent { focus, foreground[], collapse[], reason } — model may only propose

findings.deterministic_vs_generative: Deterministic compile needs the ontology up front (known shapes); generative UI guesses the shape per question and can write ad-hoc logic — value and risk (silent logic errors).

positions_taken: For repo state: deterministic and not live is preferred
Semantic UI compilation is underused in app/web dev
LLM for content and intent; deterministic compiler for form
Interesting part is interaction, not looking: UI as working state the model can see
Against the 'agent owns everything' paradigm: LLM is one module in a multi-module architecture, used only where semantic intelligence is needed (cf. Weavr)
MCP Apps is the wrong center for this — it makes the chat the owner and the state a guest; MCP belongs at the edge as an adapter

architecture.shape: Files = shared state. Editor, live view, chat agent are modules that read/render/write. LLM = a 'semantic language server', like LSP: separate, watches, contributes.
architecture.two_way_loop: state.json -> render -> user change -> typed update -> state.json (UI never owns hidden truth)
requirements: revision + identity: who wrote what on which version
architecture.conflict_rule_for_prototype: last write wins per field + revision counter (Figma-style)

ai.AG-UI / CopilotKit: bidirectional shared state via STATE_SNAPSHOT / STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch); conflicts left to implementer
ai.MCP Apps (spec 2026-01-26): ui/update-model-context — UI tells model its state, overwrites, deferred to next user message; app-only tool visibility
ai.Claude artifacts: shared artifact database Claude can read/write

prior_art.gap: Pipes and visibility exist; governance (proposal -> human confirms) is missing in AI UI protocols

open_questions: How does an LLM 'listen'? It only runs when called — what wakes it: next human message, watcher rule, schedule?
Trigger rules as deterministic code deciding when semantic intelligence is needed
Cross-device signal (Mac mini, Tailscale): git sync vs small relay server
State granularity: meaningful state (decisions, statuses, notes) over raw events
Escape hatch when content doesn't fit the catalog: AppBlock-style or text fallback?
first_experiment_candidate: Build-plan tracker: already has a state object and JSON export; add a small local server (POST -> state.json, watch -> push to page) and a revision counter.
